1521district–category screening entries
Unassessedconfirmed needs and district budgets

Desk-screen expansion of the three district starting themes. A category is included if its trigger matches a theme; overlapping categories are deduplicated by ID. This is an assessment checklist, not additional district research, a severity ranking or evidence that a problem occurs at a site. Confirmed problems, impacts and budgets remain unassessed, not zero.

Reviewed 15 October 2026 · Public planning edition · Download the field registers ↓

Number of problems per district

“Screened” counts checklist categories, not verified problem sites or severity. Multiple sites can share one problem; one site can have several problems. No “people helped” figure is claimed before delivery and verification.

Ariyalur · 10 categories to investigate

inland villages and cultivated plains. District brief and evidence routes ↗

Confirmed local problems: not assessed. These categories expand the existing desk screen. A local survey may remove or add problems.

  1. Dry-season safe-water interruption — measure People and households, Water security. Evidence guide ↗
  2. Groundwater depletion or unreliable wells — measure Water security, Farms and livelihoods. Evidence guide ↗
  3. Livestock water and fodder stress — measure Livestock, Water security. Evidence guide ↗
  4. Overheating homes and public buildings — measure People and households, Heat and buildings. Evidence guide ↗
  5. Outdoor-worker heat exposure — measure People and households, Heat and buildings. Evidence guide ↗
  6. Lost tank, wetland or flood-storage function — measure Lakes, tanks and wetlands, Water security, Floods, slopes and coasts. Evidence guide ↗
  7. Crop water stress and irrigation inefficiency — measure Farms and livelihoods, Water security. Evidence guide ↗
  8. Soil erosion and declining soil cover — measure Farms and livelihoods, Trees and habitat. Evidence guide ↗
  9. Climate-sensitive farm livelihood losses — measure People and households, Farms and livelihoods. Evidence guide ↗
  10. Loss of native canopy and poor restoration survival — measure Trees and habitat, Heat and buildings. Evidence guide ↗

People helped, animals supported, surviving trees, restored waterbodies and project budget: baseline / design pending. Record each site separately before aggregating district totals.

Impact assessment parameters

For every indicator record: site ID, baseline value and date, target, actual result and date, unit, measurement method, evidence link, verifier and uncertainty. “Proposed”, “funded”, “delivered” and “verified outcome” are different stages.

People and households

Measure: Unique direct people; unique households; disaggregate by age, gender, disability and livelihood where consent allows.

Method: Count only people with documented access to the improved service. Deduplicate across projects; report indirect reach separately.

When: Baseline, completion, 6 and 12 months

Livestock

Measure: Animals by species; households owning them; animal-days with adequate water, shade or fodder; morbidity and mortality.

Method: Use owner registers and veterinary records. Animals are not people; do not add them into a single beneficiary total.

When: Baseline and same heat/dry season after delivery

Trees and habitat

Measure: Existing trees protected; planted native trees; surviving trees at 12 and 36 months; canopy and habitat area (ha).

Method: Keep planted and surviving counts separate. Record species, plot, survival denominator and replacement trees. Avoid planting in natural grasslands or wetlands.

When: Baseline, planting, 12 and 36 months

Lakes, tanks and wetlands

Measure: Unique waterbodies; area (ha); surveyed capacity (m³); seasonal water levels; quality; functioning inlets/outlets; habitat.

Method: Assign a stable waterbody ID. Count restoration only against agreed ecological and service criteria; desilting volume is not automatically water saved.

When: Wet/dry baseline and comparable post-work seasons

Water security

Measure: People receiving safe water; service days; quality test compliance; groundwater depth; verified storage and abstraction (m³).

Method: Use laboratory results, service logs and calibrated meters; separate drinking water, irrigation and recharge. A lined pond is storage, not a recharge structure.

When: Monthly service logs; seasonal levels and quality

Farms and livelihoods

Measure: Unique farmers; hectares treated; yield, net farm income, irrigation use and crop loss.

Method: Compare equivalent crop seasons and weather; include input/labour costs and a suitable comparison group where feasible.

When: Baseline and at least two comparable crop seasons

Heat and buildings

Measure: Unique occupants; roofs treated (m²); occupied hours above an agreed heat threshold; indoor/outdoor temperature; illness.

Method: Paired sensors and occupancy records; distinguish room temperature from roof-surface temperature. Do not promise a fixed temperature reduction.

When: Before/after during comparable hot weather

Floods, slopes and coasts

Measure: Households and critical assets exposed; flood depth/duration; warning lead time; evacuation access; erosion or slope movement.

Method: Map exposure and drainage/catchment effects. Risk reduction is modelled until comparable events occur; disclose model assumptions.

When: Baseline, annual preparedness and after relevant events

Energy and emissions

Measure: Metered kWh; equipment uptime; verified fuel displaced; tCO₂e with dated emission factors.

Method: Separate generation, consumption and export; state boundary and factor. Never infer carbon sequestration from tree count alone.

When: Meter monthly; annual reconciliation

Aggregation and attribution

Deduplicate direct people within a district and across programmes using privacy-preserving local IDs. Do not sum people, animals, trees and lakes into one “impact” number. Before/after change alone does not establish that the project caused it; use comparison sites, weather adjustment or a transparent contribution assessment. Publish anonymised totals, not personal or animal-owner registers.

Waterbody assessment source

MoHUA urban waterbody rejuvenation advisory (2023) ↗ is a technical route for appraisal. Each lake needs its own catchment, pollution, hydrology and maintenance assessment; there is no universal per-lake rate in this tool.

Build a district project estimate

Select the district, define an actual site package, and enter quantities and dated low/high rates in rupees. Empty rows stay unpriced; a subtotal is not a complete budget. These are browser-only scenarios and are not saved or submitted.

Quantity × local unit rate; keep each row’s unit consistent
Work packageQuantityLow ₹ / unitHigh ₹ / unit
Assessment and design (person-days)
Safe water / livestock facilities (specified units)
Native habitat work and aftercare (specified units)
Waterbody work (measured quantities)
Heat protection / cool roofs (m²)
Farm adaptation (ha or specified units)
Lined farm ponds (ponds)
Monitoring and independent verification (person-days)
Annual operation and maintenance (years)
Permits, taxes and contingency (separate allowance)

No estimate yet. Enter a quantity and both rates.

The example uses 10 ponds × ₹1,60,000 = ₹16 lakh for construction only, using the historical NABARD Telangana 2025–26 benchmark, printed p.24 ↗. This is a hypothetical quantity, not a district plan or current quote. It applies to 20 × 20 m lined farm ponds, not lakes or groundwater recharge; no people or livestock benefits can be inferred from this arithmetic. Reprice locally for 2026–27. The example may be loaded only for a Telangana district.

How to make the estimate fundable

Confirm the unmet need and avoid overlap with existing schemes. Compare technical options, secure permissions and community consent, measure quantities, obtain dated comparable local quotes or a current schedule of rates, assign maintenance funding and include monitoring. Report capital cost, annual recurring cost, replacement provision and the selected appraisal period separately. Only divide lifecycle cost by verified unique beneficiaries or measured ecosystem outcomes; never assume beneficiaries from expenditure.

Take the assessment into the field

The problem register has one row per district–category pair; the impact template uses long-format rows for repeatable measurements. Blank values mean unassessed. Add site IDs before collecting data.
